audit.whatIsWrong: The entry attributes Sejuani's stun to the passive four times — 'she'll build Frost Armor stacks (her passive) for a stun', 'a Frost Armor stun', 'stack Frost Armor for the passive stun'. That is the wrong ability. It also never states that Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, which switches off Infernal Chains' slow entirely.
audit.why: Riot's text: Fury of the North 'grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows' and lets her 'damage a stunned enemy to shatter it'. The stun is Permafrost (E), available only once Winter's Wrath (W) has applied maximum Frost stacks. So the tell is her W hits, not her passive, and the passive is what turns that stun into her largest damage instance. Meanwhile your W slow does nothing to peel her while Frost Armor holds.
audit.corrected: Stun named as Permafrost off max Frost stacks from Winter's Wrath; Frost Armor stated as slow immunity plus the shatter; advice changed from 'don't overstay' to 'burst and leave before max stacks'.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Don't overstay in a prolonged auto-trade' gives no window to count.
audit.why: Winter's Wrath is 9/8/7/6/5s and Permafrost is a flat 1.5s gated on stacks, so the real clock is her W casts, not a cooldown you can wait out.
audit.corrected: Trade rule now keyed to her Winter's Wrath hits reaching max Frost.

edits.before: Your window — Sejuani is a tank with weak early damage. Once you have Q pattern + W, brawl her down: W-pull, Q-sweetspot, E drain. She'll build Frost Armor stacks (her passive) for a stun, so don't overstay in a prolonged auto-trade; burst her in windows and reset.
edits.after: Your window — Sejuani is a tank with weak early damage. Once you have Q pattern + W, brawl her down: chain, Q-sweetspot, E drain. Winter's Wrath stacks Frost until Permafrost stuns and her passive shatters you, so burst and leave before she reaches max stacks.

edits.before: From level 3 you take over — Sejuani is a low-damage tank and your combo plus drain simply out-brawl her. W-pull her in, land the Q sweetspot knockup, and E-drain, but be aware she stacks Frost Armor (her passive) toward a stun in long trades, so hit your burst windows and reset rather than standing in an extended auto-fight. At 6, respect Glacial Prison as a gank setup — hold E to dodge her Arctic Assault engage and R to out-sustain her chip. Your all-in wins; her jungle is the danger.
edits.after: From level 3 you take over — Sejuani is a low-damage tank and your combo plus drain out-brawl her. Chain her in, land the third-Q knockup, E-drain, but count her Winter's Wrath hits: at max Frost, Permafrost stuns and Fury of the North shatters you for the biggest hit she owns. Frost Armor is also slow-immune, so your W will not peel her — burst in windows and leave. At 6 respect Glacial Prison as gank setup, and hold Umbral Dash for her Arctic Assault engage rather than for chase.

edits.before: Your item spike lets you keep shredding her even through her armor stacking, and since she has almost no solo kill pressure you can farm her out — just don't dive into a Frost Armor stun under tower. Late game Sejuani becomes elite teamfight engage with her R and Permafrost detonations, so lane priority evens to a wash: she wins the utility war, you win any isolated 1v1. Split-push and force her to answer you alone, away from her team, where her CC does nothing.

edits.before: Sejuani changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Sejuani Q, E/passive, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Sejuani wants to survive lane, farm safely, stack durability, and become more valuable in later fights than the early lane suggests.
edits.after: Sejuani changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Winter's Wrath stacking Frost until Permafrost (E) stuns and Fury of the North shatters him. Aatrox wins by spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, holding Umbral Dash for her Arctic Assault, and bursting out before max stacks. Sejuani wants to survive lane, stack durability, and be worth more in later fights than the lane suggests.
